Chapter 8: How to Build and Sustain the Circle of Safety
Building a Circle of Safety isn't about making big, flashy changes or introducing sweeping policies. It's actually about the small, everyday moments that might even go unnoticed—the kind of moments where you simply show up for each other. The best leaders? They know trust gets built in those tiny interactions. Maybe it's a kind word, really listening when someone speaks, or being brave enough to admit when you've messed up.
Imagine a nonprofit team, constantly juggling tight budgets and huge ambitions. The director doesn’t just check in about the latest project. She makes time to ask about everyone’s life outside the office. When someone’s having a rough week, the team steps up—covering shifts, pitching in on projects, whatever it takes. There’s this silent agreement: we’re on the same side. Even when things get challenging, folks stick around, because deep down, they know they matter.
But here’s something to pay attention to—most organizations miss the magic in these everyday connections. They chase after numbers and performance reviews, forgetting that people need to feel noticed, to feel heard. When leaders slow down and really connect, trust doesn’t just appear—it grows. Suddenly, people open up with new ideas, they’re willing to take risks, and they’ve got each other’s backs.
Now, keeping that Circle of Safety strong takes real effort. Old habits like competition, blame, and secrecy can sneak back in, especially when stress is high. That’s when leaders need to double down on the message: we’re in this together, and what happens to one of us affects all of us. Maybe that means celebrating what the team accomplishes as a whole, instead of just calling out one superstar. Or maybe it’s about being honest when things aren’t going well, instead of pretending everything’s fine.
I love this example from a company that started every meeting with a round of gratitude. Each person would share something they appreciated about a teammate. At first, it probably felt a little awkward, maybe even cheesy. But over time? It completely changed how people treated each other. Arguments got settled faster, and teamwork really took off.
Most of us don’t realize just how much these little rituals matter. They’re the glue that keeps the Circle of Safety together, especially when the going gets tough.
